lede: Nations that called the Hour a lie; the Hour itself, with eight bearing the Throne above it; a man holding up his record and calling, “Here — read my book!”; and then the most solemn oath in the Qurʾan that these are not a poet’s words.

names.name: al-Ḥāqqah
names.note: One of the names of the Day of Resurrection, and the surah’s first word. Ibn Kathīr explains it: because in it the promise and the threat are made real.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all: both Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī record the agreement. The traditional order places it seventy-eighth, immediately after al-Mulk.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الحاقَّةِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
الحاقةُ مِنْ أَسْمَاءِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ؛ لِأَنَّ فِيهَا يَتَحقَّقُ الوَعدُ والوَعيد؛ وَلِهَذَا عَظَّم تَعَالَى أمرَها

setting: No occasion is transmitted for the surah. It answers the two things Quraysh said most often in those years: that there would be no Resurrection, and that the Qurʾan was the work of a poet or a soothsayer.

To the first it replies with history they knew. Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Striking Calamity. Thamūd were destroyed by the overwhelming blast; ʿĀd by a screaming, violent wind that He loosed on them for seven nights and eight days without a break, until you could see the people lying like hollow trunks of palm. Pharaoh, and those before him, and the overturned cities. And the Flood: “When the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship.”

To the second it replies by oath — by all that you see and all that you do not see — that this is the word of a noble messenger, not a poet’s, not a soothsayer’s, but sent down from the Lord of the worlds. And then a sentence that only the truth could afford to say: had he invented any saying in Our name, We would have seized him by the right hand and cut his life-vein, and not one of you could have shielded him.

A report in the Musnad of Aḥmad has ʿUmar, before his Islam, standing behind the Prophet ﷺ at the Kaʿbah and hearing this surah; each time he thought, “a poet,” or “a soothsayer,” the next ayah answered him. Its chain is broken — the narrator did not meet ʿUmar — so it is told as a report and not as established.
aim: That the Resurrection must come to pass — confirming the truth of the Qurʾan, promising the believers their joy, and threatening the deniers with their regret.

outline.title: Those who denied it
outline.summary: The Inevitable Reality — what is the Inevitable Reality? Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Striking Calamity: Thamūd were destroyed by the overwhelming blast, and ʿĀd by a furious wind, seven nights and eight days on end. Pharaoh, and those before him, and the overthrown cities. And when the water rose, We carried you in the ship, to make it a reminder for you.

outline.title: The Day itself
outline.summary: When the Trumpet is blown with a single blast, and the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single blow — on that Day the Event will come to pass. The sky will split; the angels will be at its edges; and eight, that Day, will bear the Throne of your Lord above them. That Day you will be brought out; nothing of yours will stay hidden.

outline.title: The book in the right hand
outline.summary: He will say, “Here — read my record! I was sure that I would meet my reckoning.” He will be in a life of contentment, in a lofty garden whose fruit hangs near. “Eat and drink with pleasure, for what you sent ahead in the days gone by.”

outline.title: The book in the left
outline.summary: He will say, “If only I had never been given my record, and never known my reckoning. If only that death had been the end. My wealth has not availed me; my authority has left me.” Seize him and shackle him; then burn him in the Blaze; then bind him in a chain of seventy cubits. He did not believe in Allah, the Tremendous, nor urge the feeding of the poor.

outline.title: Whose word this is
outline.summary: I swear by what you see and what you do not see: it is the word of a noble messenger — not the word of a poet, little do you believe; nor of a soothsayer, little do you reflect. A sending down from the Lord of the worlds. Had he fabricated sayings against Us, We would have seized him by the right hand and severed his aorta. It is a reminder for the mindful, and it is the truth of certainty. So glorify the name of your Lord, the Tremendous.

keyAyah.why: The moment of joy the whole surah is leading the believer towards — a person so glad of his record that he wants everyone to read it.

virtuesNote: Al-Qurṭubī cites a report that whoever recites eleven ayat of this surah will be protected from the Dajjāl. That protection is established for the opening of al-Kahf, in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; nothing sound is transmitted of it for al-Ḥāqqah.
before: Al-Qalam said that the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew (68:33). Al-Ḥāqqah opens by naming it, and asking what could make you know what it is.
after: Al-Maʿārij continues with a man who asked for that very punishment to fall, and with the length of the Day on which it will.

notable.label: Eight will bear the Throne of your Lord

Had he invented anything in Our name
